transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-15
Start time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Omar Vasquez (Redwood SE), Priya Raman (Horizon - Head of Platform), Liam O'Connor (Horizon - Infra Eng), Sofia Alvarez (Horizon - Procurement)

Summary:
Quick renewal/expansion check: Horizon wants to add EU edge nodes for lower latency to EU clinics, bump committed capacity, and finalize contract extension terms. Conversation covered technical validation (throughput/latency), security/compliance checklist, procurement timeline, and pricing tiers. Action items and dates captured.

Topics:
- EU edge provisioning profile and expected latency improvements
- Dedicated vs Hosted capacity tradeoffs and burst handling
- Compliance (data residency, SOC2, KMS) and audit log access
- Budget and procurement timeline

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you squeezing this in. Quick roll call — Maya from Redwood, Omar our solutions engineer, and who do we have on the Horizon side?
[00:07] Priya Raman: Hi Maya, Priya here. Liam and Sofia are on as well.
[00:10] Liam O'Connor: Hey all.
[00:12] Sofia Alvarez: Hi.
[00:14] Maya Chen: Great. The agenda for today is pretty narrow: talk through the EU edge provisioning, sizing uplift, and lock in next steps for procurement. Should be 30-ish minutes but we kept 45 just in case.
[00:28] Omar Vasquez: Quick add — I'll run through the perf expectations and the pilot plan, then we can mark specific numbers for the proposal.
[00:35] Priya Raman: Sounds good. Quick context — we've been on Redwood hosted for 9 months, about 8M tokens / month now, ramping. Our clinics in Ireland and Germany are complaining about 200-300ms tail latency for chat workflows. We want EU edge to shave that down and also make sure logs + patient data don't cross regions.
[00:52] Maya Chen: Got it. So two asks: both latency and data residency. From pricing side you're interested in committed uplift and maybe a dedicated pool in EU?
[01:01] Priya Raman: Yes, committed uplift. Dedicated if the numbers justify it. Procurement also needs predictable monthly invoices — PO-based.
[01:08] Sofia Alvarez: And we do have an internal requirement for KMS integration and audit logs to be retained for 7 years, if that matters.
[01:16] Omar Vasquez: Okay, on the technical front — EU edge in our setup is a Private control plane with customer VPC peering and on-prem like network isolation, so traffic and model inference stay in the EU region. The expected improvement: median token latency drops by roughly 40-60% for the clinic routes, and 95th percentile should fall from that 200-300ms range down to ~70-120ms depending on model size and prompt length.
[01:40] Liam O'Connor: That's promising. How do you handle KV cache and prefix caching for short chat sessions? We see a lot of repeated flows so cache hit rate matters for cost.
[01:50] Omar Vasquez: We do prefix/K V cache —sorry, KV cache — automatically for session-based workloads. For high hit rates we see per-token cost drop significantly because the runtime avoids re-computing big chunks. We'll include cache hit metrics in the benchmark.
[02:03] Priya Raman: Can you guarantee that the PII won't leave the EU site? We need contractual language for data residency.
[02:10] Maya Chen: We can commit to region-bound inference in the contract for the EU edge deployment and include the KMS key residency requirement. I'll flag legal to add the clause.
[02:18] Sofia Alvarez: And SOC2? We need the right attestation and evidence for auditors.
[02:22] Maya Chen: Redwood is SOC2 Type II — we'll share the most recent report and a redacted copy for procurement.
[02:28] Liam O'Connor: On capacity — what are the options? We don't want to overcommit but also want predictable latency during peaks.
[02:35] Omar Vasquez: Typical choices: (1) Hosted burstable with region routing — lowest commitment but variable tail latency; (2) Dedicated reserved capacity in EU — predictable throughput + latency SLOs, higher commitment; (3) Hybrid: reserved baseline with burst to hosted in emergencies, with routing/fallback policies. For Horizon, given clinic SLAs, I'd recommend reserved baseline plus limited burst buffer.
[02:56] Priya Raman: What about canary rollouts? We run nightly retrain cycles and need to pin model versions on deploys.
[03:03] Omar Vasquez: We support model version pinning and canary rollouts with automatic fallback to previous model on regressions. Also quality monitoring hooks tied to evals. We'll show how the rollout looks in the console.
[03:12] Maya Chen: Budget question — what are typical pricing deltas for dedicated vs hosted for this scale?
[03:18] Omar Vasquez: Ballpark: dedicated baseline is about 30-40% cheaper per-token at scale because of amortized GPU costs, but it requires a minimum monthly commit. Bursting to hosted rate is higher per token; we can include a blended worksheet.
[03:30] Sofia Alvarez: Our procurement will need three-tier pricing: minimal, expected, and max commitment scenarios.
[03:35] Maya Chen: We'll prepare a three-tier commitment/pricing worksheet. I'll include a scenario with baseline dedicated + 20% burst, and one with hosted-only burst.
[03:44] Priya Raman: On security: we use Azure for EU, want VNet peering and our KMS. Are those integrations supported?
[03:51] Omar Vasquez: Yes, we support Azure VNet peering for Private deployments and customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations. There's a setup window for key rotation and access controls, but it's supported.
[04:02] Liam O'Connor: If we do dedicated, what's the provisioning lead time for EU GPUs?
[04:06] Maya Chen: Typically 4-8 weeks depending on capacity and exact instance type, but we can fast-track certain customers with prior notice. For a pilot we can do a smaller footprint within 2-3 weeks using shared reserved capacity and then ramp.
[04:17] Priya Raman: Good to know. Omar, you mentioned benchmarks — what's in the benchmark deliverable?
[04:21] Omar Vasquez: We'll do a 24-hour sustained throughput run on EU edge config, capture P50/P90/P99 latencies, token throughput, cache hit rates, memory pressure, and cost per 1k tokens. We'll also run a failover test to hosted to validate fallbacks.
[04:35] Priya Raman: Excellent. How exhaustive is the audit log? We need user-level tracing for compliance.
[04:41] Maya Chen: You get request-level audit logs, model version, token counts, requester id, and optional redaction markers. Logs can be exported to your SIEM/S3. We'll include retention options to meet 7-year requirement but note there are storage implications on pricing.
[04:56] Sofia Alvarez: Storage costs are fine if the feature exists, need estimate though.
[04:59] Omar Vasquez: We'll include a ballpark for log storage in the worksheet.
[05:03] [05:03] Liam O'Connor: Slight tangent — what about model quantization? We sometimes trade a bit of quality for cost.
[05:08] Omar Vasquez: We recommend quantized variants for non-latency-sensitive routes. For chat clinician-facing flows where quality matters, use FP or higher-precision variants. Redwood Optimize will give model/quantization recs by workload.
[05:21] Priya Raman: Timeline — procurement wants to finalize by end of January. Is that realistic?
[05:26] Maya Chen: If we get confirmations this week — pricing acceptance and your compliance doc — legal and procurement can aim for signature by Jan 29. It's tight but feasible.
[05:35] Sofia Alvarez: We need the official pricing doc and SOC2 copy to share with legal first.
[05:39] Maya Chen: We'll send both.
[05:41] [06:00] Omar Vasquez: Quick note about SLOs — if you pick dedicated we'll agree on latency targets per route and have a monitoring dashboard with token-level cost breakdown.
[06:11] Priya Raman: For the pilot, can we do a limited dedicated pool for one EU region and route 30% of traffic there to validate?
[06:18] Omar Vasquez: Yes, that's the recommended pilot. We can route by suffix or route keys to split traffic. We'll provide the routing config example.
[06:26] Liam O'Connor: About failover — if EU hits capacity and we fall back to hosted, is data still kept in-region?
[06:32] Maya Chen: Fall back will route to a compatible model in the assigned fallback region. We can set policies to avoid cross-border fallback; if you require strict locality then fallbacks can be configured to either queue or return error instead of crossing borders.
[06:45] Priya Raman: We might opt to queue rather than cross-border to avoid residency violations. I'll confirm.
[06:50] Sofia Alvarez: Procurement wants monthly invoicing and net-30. Is that standard?
[06:55] Maya Chen: Net-30 is commonly supported for enterprise customers, we'll include it in the contract.
[06:59] Sofia Alvarez: Any competitors we should be aware of — we talked to Anthropic and looked at Bedrock cost estimates.
[07:05] Maya Chen: Understood. We'll make sure the worksheet highlights where Redwood wins on predictable throughput and observability.
[07:10] Priya Raman: One more technical — do you support canary evaluation hooks so we can run our eval cases on new model?
[07:16] Omar Vasquez: Yes, functionally the console supports eval sets, and we can hook your test-suite to trigger canary promotion only after passing thresholds.
[07:24] Maya Chen: Ok let's summarize next steps and dates — Omar will run the 24h EU perf and share artifacts by Jan 22, Maya sends pricing tiers + SOC2 by Jan 19, Horizon shares compliance matrix by Jan 20, procurement follows up to start PO process week of Jan 26.
[07:42] Priya Raman: That aligns with internal timeline.
[07:45] Sofia Alvarez: Yep.
[07:46] Liam O'Connor: One quick ask — can Omar also include a sample routing policy for 30/70 split?
[07:51] Omar Vasquez: Yep will include that in the benchmark package.
[07:54] [08:30] Maya Chen: Great. Any blockers we didn't cover?
[08:33] Priya Raman: None besides legal review of residency clause.
[08:36] Sofia Alvarez: Procurement side is okay to start once we have pricing and SOC2.
[08:39] Maya Chen: Perfect. Thanks all, we'll follow up with the artifacts.
[08:44] Priya Raman: Thank you.
[08:45] Meeting end.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-attribution and filler words; some acronyms may be expanded incorrectly (K V cache etc.).

Attachments referenced:

- EU edge benchmark plan (Omar)

Recap (short):
- Pilot: 30% traffic to EU edge pilot, 24h perf run, follow up by Jan 22
- Contract: three-tier pricing worksheet and SOC2 to Horizon by Jan 19, aim for signature by Jan 29
- Compliance: Horizon to share data residency matrix by Jan 20

End of transcript.
